blocks.text: Inflammatory arthritis refers to a group of diseases characterized by inflammation of the joints, including:

RA is a chronic, systemic autoimmune disease that primarily affects synovial joints, causing symmetrical inflammation, pain, and progressive joint deformity. It often involves the hands and feet, but any synovial joint may be affected. Extra-articular manifestations (such as those affecting the skin, heart, lungs, and eyes) can also occur.

Heart Failure (HF) (NYHA III/IV): Prefer non-TNF bDMARDs or tsDMARDs over TNF inhibitors if csDMARDs fail or HF develops.
Pulmonary Disease: MTX is acceptable in mild, stable lung disease or incidental findings.
Lymphoproliferative Disorder: Rituximab is preferred if there is a history of treated lymphoproliferative disease.
HBsAg-positive: Use rituximab with prophylactic antivirals.

Cardiovascular disease: Tofacitinib is contraindicated in patients with a history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or HF.

PsA is a chronic inflammatory arthritis that is usually seen in patients with psoriasis, although it may predate skin involvement, which can be subtle. It typically presents as seronegative oligoarthritic, with features such as distal joint involvement, arthritis mutilans, or inflammation of joints, spine, entheses, nails, and skin.

Enteropathic arthritis is a seronegative spondyloarthritis associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). It can involve both the axial skeleton (spine and sacroiliac joints) and the peripheral joints, and may also present with enthesitis or dactylitis.
